drills.title: Three ways to write one function
hints: Check the type of a function of x : Nat and y : Bool returning x + 1 if y is false and x + 2 otherwise (using `not`), written as one lambda over x whose body is a lambda over y, each binder type-annotated.
Check the same function again, as a single lambda binding both annotated arguments at once.
Check it a third time, as a single lambda over x and y with no type annotations at all, leaving Lean to infer them.

drills.title: Chaining local definitions
hints: Check the type of an expression that locally defines y as 2 + 2, then z as y + y, and returns z * z, all on one line.
Evaluate that same expression.

drills.title: Composing functions with variables
hints: Declare variables α, β, γ, each a Type.
Declare variables g : β → γ, f : α → β, and h : α → α.
Declare a variable x : α.
Define `compose` as g applied to f applied to x, with no explicit parameters.
Define `doTwice` as h applied twice to x.
Define `doThrice` as h applied three times to x.
Print the definitions of compose, doTwice, and doThrice.

drills.title: Scoping variables to a section
hints: Open a section named `useful`.
Inside it, declare variables α, β, γ, each a Type.
Declare variables g : β → γ, f : α → β, and h : α → α.
Declare a variable x : α.
Define `compose` as g applied to f applied to x, `doTwice` as h applied twice to x, and `doThrice` as h applied three times to x, none with explicit parameters.
Close the section.

drills.title: Short names from the List namespace
hints: Open the List namespace.
Check nil, cons, and map by their short names.

drills.title: Defining in and reopening a namespace
hints: Open a namespace named Foo.
Define `a : Nat` as 5.
Define `f`, taking x : Nat and returning the Nat x + 7.
Define `fa : Nat` as f applied to a, referring to both by their short names.
Close the namespace.
Check Foo.a and Foo.f by their full names.
Reopen Foo, define `ffa : Nat` as f applied twice to a, and close it again.

drills.title: Full types of List functions
hints: Check the types of List.cons, List.nil, List.length, and List.append, each with all of its implicit arguments made explicit.

drills.title: Building and projecting dependent pairs
hints: Declare universe levels u and v.

Define `f` with parameters α : Type u, β : α → Type v, a : α, and b : β a, returning the dependent pair type over a : α of β a, written in the binder-product form; build the pair from a and b with the anonymous constructor.
Define `g` with the same parameters, but write its return type with the Σ notation and build the pair with Sigma.mk.
Define `h1`, taking x : Nat and returning a Nat: apply f to Type, the identity type family (a lambda over α returning α), Nat, and x, then take the second component of the result.
Evaluate h1 on 5.
Define `h2` the same way as h1 but using g instead of f.
Evaluate h2 on 5.

drills.title: A universe-polymorphic identity function
hints: Declare a universe level u.
Define `ident`, taking a type α : Type u as an implicit argument and an explicit x : α, and returning x; leave the return type unstated.

drills.title: Identity from implicit section variables
hints: Declare a universe u.
Open an anonymous section.
Inside it, declare α : Type u as an implicit section variable.
Then declare x : α as an explicit section variable.
Define `ident` to be x.
Close the section.
Check the type of ident, then of ident applied to 4, then of ident applied to "hello".
